quest.title: Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu
quest.description: Little Mao seems to have some information about how to help heal Chenyu Vale...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Looks like there's another realm in here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hilichurls! Get behind us, Mao!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hehe... Stuff like this happens sometimes, but my friend would always chase them away, so... I'm not scared at all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your friend must be pretty strong... Could she be some sorta adeptus too...?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Well... I wouldn't say so. In fact, she forbade me from talking about her willy-nilly, so... Well, sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Come on, no need to apologize!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: This is it! It's the clue I wanted to show you before, right here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What on Teyvat is that? It's so covered in moss that Paimon can't make heads or tails of it.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Ehhh? There wasn't any moss the last time I came here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No need to worry, Little Mao! It's so humid here that it's no wonder there's moss growing everywhere. Hmm, there must be a way to clear it away...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}, look! It's a scene of ancient people attending a festival and performing a ritual. Pretty different from the festivals we have today, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Although the grown-ups in the city and the village all say that the Lord of Geo was the first to arrive in Chenyu Vale, I've heard that the people in the picture actually got here even earlier than he did!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: People back then used to throw bits of magic jade into the river, and they'd float along until they sank to the bottom. They saw it as a way to guarantee good weather, prevent the river from flooding, and ensure that the soil would be fertile.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Based on what we previously discussed, I'm guessing that Chenyu Vale will only be fixed after we've found some jade that was thrown into the river in ancient times! That makes sense, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're so knowledgeable! Was your friend also the one who told you these stories?

choices.text: You rule, Little Mao! That's first-class guide material right there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Little Mao's a local, so of course he understands this place better than Paimon!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Yep, and... Everyone'll be really blessed and live happily ever after, and all that...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe, but I much prefer hearing her stories about ancient wars and battles... She told me that the warriors back then were all giants who were over ten feet tall!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: The warriors of Chenyu Vale were covered in tattoos, and they had these massive jade axes that could chop a person in half in the blink of an eye!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: And the Millelith, led by none other than the Lord of Geo himself, were even tougher! They clad themselves in suits of armor that weighed over a thousand pounds and fought with hundred-pound spears! Apparently, everyone was at war back then, so much so that Bishui River turned crimson red...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Later on, the mountains to the south became full of ghosts from that era. Even now, those who wander through the mountains might still be able to catch their singing on the wind...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ergh...

choices.text: Yikes, scary stuff! Cover your ears, Mini Pie.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, who's Mini Pie? Hautemontagne's right though — if you constantly think about this stuff, you'll turn into a villain when you're older!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe... There's no way grown-ups would tell us these stories. They always say we're too young to hear them, that they'll turn us rotten, and stuff like that.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: But I'm old enough already! Hearing a story's not going to turn me into a monster. Besides, there aren't many adults still around who know these stories anyway. If my friend hadn't told me, I wouldn't even have known the stories about this picture!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, fine then, guess we'll move on.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: So... the grown-ups were right to say that those ancient people threw the jade into the river from somewhere high up... but where exactly? And where did all the jade float off to...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Well, it must have sunk to the bottom, right?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: It's not that simple... If it was thrown in somewhere upriver, and even if it sank to the bottom, it would still be pushed downriver by the current. Let alone after so many years...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Besides, I've never heard talk of any ancient ritual jade being found upriver... Chenyu Vale is a small place, after all. If there had been such rumors, everyone would already know about them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you know so much. You're future scholar material for sure!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe... But what if I don't want to be a scholar? They don't earn much Mora, and it sounds like no fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then become a traveler, just like us! What could be more fun than adventuring around the world?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hmm... Seeing as we now know the site of the Rainjade Rite, what should we do next?

choices.text: Why don't we go somewhere high up to take a look?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: High up, hmm... The watchtower at Yilong Wharf's pretty high up!

choices.text: Okay, let's head out.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Alright! Let's go!

choices.text: I want to take another look around.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Okay! Let me know when you're ready.

choices.text: Let's observe how the river flows.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: If we want to see how the river flows...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe it would be a good idea to try the tall watchtower over at Yilong Wharf?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe, you're a clever one, Ms. Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, of course!

choices.text: Okay, let's head out.
I want to take another look around.
I don't think these stories are meant for kids...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... It sounds terrifying! Hautemontagne's right, you shouldn't dwell on this stuff all the time.

choices.text: These legends are fascinating.

talks.objective: Go to the watchtower at Yilong Wharf

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Look! From up here, you can clearly see how the water moves faster through those narrows, then slows down again as the river widens out. The jade must have stopped there! We should find what we're looking for there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're such a real whiz-kid! Paimon's been wondering though... What's that massive thing in the distance?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: That huge thing is the Jademouth, a legendary "jade ring" that an adeptus threw into the water!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Oh... But the river curves around there, so the current should actually speed up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the river gradually gets wider there.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Yeah, so the rapid flow around the bend might have resulted in things being deposited along the convex bank where it widens... So there's actually a good chance that the jade is at the bottom of the river somewhere around Jademouth. Of course, that's assuming that the course of the river hasn't been artificially altered!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hmm, not to mention... There's a fisherman's legend that goes something like... "Jade shall rise from sunken mouth"... or something like that. Anyway, let's go over and take a look around first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Compared to Little Mao, Paimon feels like she's completely out of her depth...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's because my friend is amazing! She knows everything there is to know about the mountains, and she's taught me loads too — that's how I've learned so much.

choices.text: Sorry, Paimon. You just need better friends!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Uhh, that's not what I meant! I mean, you unblocked the cave and got rid of that moss in a flash, after all, and I have no idea how you even did that!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm just kidding, don't overthink it.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Whatever the case, let's go down and get on a bamboo raft!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hoho, yeah! Jademouth, here we come!

choices.text: #You are unfit for duty, Mini Pie. As the {M#Young Master}{F#Young Lady}, I am most disappointed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...{NICKNAME}, has the rarefied mountain air or miasma gone to your head or something? Or does the adeptal energy you used have side effects? You're behaving pretty strangely...

choices.text: Don't worry too much about it, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... That's right! Paimon has lots of other strengths...

talks.objective: Board the bamboo raft and go to the Jademouth

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Someone coming aboard? ...Wait, is that Little Mao? Come, come, I'll take you!

talks.objective: Listen to stories of the past

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: We're here, this is the Jademouth!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Such a huge hunk of jade, and even the other pieces on it are massive! Whoever it was that threw it down, adeptus or not, must have been absolutely titanic!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hehe, adepti come in all shapes and sizes. "They could be as tall as the clouds, or small enough to hide amidst pool and leaf..." Agh, how did the rest of it go again... anyway, you get the picture! To sum up, adepti rule!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here's the Jademouth. But how are we gonna find all that jade underwater?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's how it is. "...The spring's cries ripple through the vales, the shrines depart from northeast shores..."

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: "The heights and shallows in the southwest hide, sun and earth from each other divide, the eternal whirlpool that never churns, the beautiful jade concealed within..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that Little Mao's singing about? It sounds pretty complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: It's one of our local folksongs, I heard an old granny singing it as she was gathering herbs! It means... If you look out from the center of the river to the banks on either side, you'll see two stone shrines hidden to the northeast and the southwest. These shrines keep the mighty whirlpool in the center suppressed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon understood the last bit! So the jade is all hidden beneath the whirlpool?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Yep! Sounds like we're going treasure hunting, hooray!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the area between the northeast and southwest is so huge! After all, in a broad sense, the northeast and southwest of Jademouth can include... pretty much the whole world?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: You're always thinking outside the box, Ms. Paimon! But there's no need to worry, I already have an idea where the shrines will be, because... Well, my friend told me! Come on, let's roll.

choices.text: I have a question...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Does anyone else think a giant maelstrom suddenly appearing here might not be too great?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! Won't that mean that boats will no longer be able to sail in and out of Yilong Wharf?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Oh, don't worry about that! My friend told me that once we've done what we need to beneath, the whirlpool will disappear completely! Otherwise, how would all the old boatmen carry on making a living?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so it's not just a smart whirlpool, but a considerate one to boot! Let's get going then!

choices.text: Hold up for a second...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Huh. We haven't seen the whirlpool from the song yet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What should we do next?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #How about... Giving that "adeptal energy" of yours a try, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, we meet again. And who might this be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You haven't met before? This is Little Mao, he's helped us so much along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: No, we haven't met before. But you must be a good child, Little Mao.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hello, and yes, that's me! Miss, are you... an adeptus? You are, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is Adeptus Fujin.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #Hehe, thanks for all the help you've given {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Little Mao.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: It's really the legendary Fujin, in the flesh! I can't believe this, I've heard so many stories about you! And... Now I know that you're not some kind of big, slippery Carp, but a lady instead, like a big sister!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—Big Carp!? Honestly, what kind of stories have you been listening to, Little Mao?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Ahem...! One is indeed an adeptus, and as such, can take forms as one pleases. This particular form seemed like the most approachable one for conversing with humans...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Hmm, from what you've said... You have a very unique scent, Little Mao. Have you met someone in the mountains before? Someone with golden eyes and a fair complexion, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Uh, not exactly... Big Sis Fujin, you're not talking about one of your other friends, are you? My friend from the mountains doesn't sparkle like you do, but she's also really cool! She's helped me tons and taught me loads...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: So it was her after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So your friend wasn't Adeptus Fujin after all, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: But Big Sis Fujin's my friend too now, isn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Of course, Little Mao! I am delighted to have made friends with you.

choices.text: Way to go, Little Mao! You've now met two adepti...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...But I've met more! Whoop whoop, go me! I win!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Huh? Wha...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uhh... Don't worry about {F#her}{M#him}. Anyway, does that mean Little Mao's friend is also an adeptus?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: As for whether Little Mao's friend counts as an adeptus or not... I'm not quite sure myself. After all, "adeptus" is merely a title — and it's hard to say whether adepti are even "people."

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: The word "adeptus" is just like any other word, such as "hero," "villain," or "idiot"... No one is born an adeptus, and no one shall remain an adeptus forever.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true... So you've met that friend of Little Mao's that we were talking about, right?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Indeed. But it's been a long, long time since last I saw her. So now... I suspect that I don't know her half as well as Little Mao does. I'm not even sure if I still count as her friend.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: According to what Little Mao said...

choices.text: His "friend" wants to restore nature.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...I would imagine so.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Anyway, I must ask you all to please take this piece of "Votive Rainjade." I had originally hoped it might remain here, the same as it ever was, but I never expected it to grow quite so large... *sigh* I used to love it so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This "Rainjade" that you just mentioned... Did it rain down, or make it rain, or something...?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Hehe, of course not. After the great changes in our geology, our... the ancestors of the people of Chenyu Vale lost their ability to communicate with the heavens, and lost the guidance of emissaries whose beauty was pure as moonlight.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Henceforth, they began to take jade, which glowed as gently as the light of the moon, and cast it into the river. As they did this, they would pray for good omens, for fertile land, for clement weather, and for their riverbanks to hold strong. Over time, these rituals grew in power, until one day...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: One day...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Big Sis Fujin? What happened next?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...One day, the long war to become the gods who would reign over this world began. Afterward, this tradition lost all of its meaning. But though it was forgotten, its name is still passed down over generations.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: To cut a long story short, this piece of Votive Rainjade before us... Was the very last one ever to be thrown.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Just as the part above the surface — when commanded by an adeptal art — can be made large enough to stop a flood, its core, too, has been swollen by uncontrolled adeptal energy. Much of its power has dissipated into the surrounding area through the spirit veins.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: This power may also have affected the nearby flora and fauna, attracting and even making aberrations of them. You must be careful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: As far as I can tell, the adeptal energy that has dissipated nearby should be sufficient to re-awaken the hibernating Votive Rainjade. If this is the case, we're one step closer to achieving our goal of nursing the water and soil back to health.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Ahem, how should I say this? {NICKNAME} and Paimon... thank you both. You're doing an amazing thing by choosing to help me, you know. And Little Mao... Will you help me too? Will you help out your Big Sis?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Of course, I want to restore nature too!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...Is that so? Well that's good. You're very smart, Little Mao! You'll understand everything later.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Alright, then let us go our separate ways for now.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Once you've retrieved the adeptal energy-filled Votive Rainjade, we'll meet again by a deep pool shrouded in cloud and mist to the south.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The south... Got it! Eh...? She's gone and disappeared again!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Ah well! Let's just do what Big Sis Fujin said and restore this Voting Rainjade's power!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Speaking of which... What's it got to do with voting?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, see! You're not that much brighter than Paimon, hmph!

choices.text: It's "Votive."

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Oh, right...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: It's so complicated!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though, since you mentioned it... What does "Votive" even mean? And why is it called "Rainjade" again?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Exactly! What does it mean!?

choices.text: Not "Voting."
His "friend" wants to restore nature too.
Little Mao's met other adepti?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Seems like the jade's starting to move...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: That's right. But according to the story, the riverbed should have lots of other Votive Rainjades. Why does Big Sis Fujin only want this one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Look! It's shining, almost as if it's resonating with the adeptal energy on you, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't we try using that power, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: That should do it. Wow, awesome! It suddenly became small!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Paimon didn't think it'd just change size like that. Guess that's a millennia-old treasure for you... It's just like you said, Little Mao! "They could be as tall as the clouds, or small enough to hide amidst pool and leaf..."

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Yeah! Well, looks like the Votive Rainjade's in our hands now. You're so reliable, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon worked hard too!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Ms. Paimon's amazing! So you're going to take us to that "deep pool shrouded in cloud and mist to the south" now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Clouds and mist... Hmm... I think Chenyu Vale really does have places like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where? Tell us, little guide, and Paimon'll take you there!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Do you remember the place Mountain mentioned, the spot where we met? That place is super foggy, and I know of a secret cavern that leads there. Even the other locals don't know about it.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: It was my friend who showed me the way, and since you're my friend too, Paimon, I'll tell you all about it!

choices.text: You've got an amazing friend, Little Mao.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe, of course. Uh, well, you're both pretty impressive too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, any friend of yours is a friend of ours too! In fact, Paimon hopes we'll meet her on the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shall we go? Paimon's gonna take you all to the... place you mentioned, Little Mao!

choices.text: Take us away, Ms. Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty then. Let's go!

choices.text: Give me a moment. Let's see if there are any treasure chests that we haven't found yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously? There's no helping you, huh? Hang on a moment, alright, Little Mao?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Okay! The cavern's pretty dark, so you've gotta be careful!

choices.text: Your friend in the mountains... Are they connected to Adeptus Fujin?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: ...She's told me lots of stories, and quite a few of them were about Big Sis Fujin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're the one who needs to be careful... Paimon can fly, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Watch your step... There's moss on the cliff, it's slippery!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, slow down!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Here, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Wow, she's... she really was right about you. You're pretty out of the ordinary.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess that settles it!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Wow, you're amazing! Even my friend couldn't do anything about the shrines!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you got that right!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Wow! And just like the legend says, a Golden Carp!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so it's Adeptus Fujin again!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: "Fujin"?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the river breeze blows, you hitch a ride on the rocking bamboo raft,\nAnd you slowly reach the Jademouth.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Here we are. There's a cavern behind this waterfall. Try not to get soaked, you might catch a cold!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Eh? It's blocked off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um, how about you give that "adeptal energy" a go, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: There's more water in here than before. Maybe I'll have to swim in next time.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Look at that bamboo raft. Guess we've got a boat we can take now!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Alright, boatman, take us to the Jademouth!

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Alright, Jademouth it is! The other two, you're... tourists? Haha, well if you're here for sightseeing, there's not many locals who head that way.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hehe, you could say that! Mr. Boatman, are there any stories about the Jademouth that I haven't heard before?

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Knowing you and how much you love your stories, kiddo, you must have heard them all by now!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Tell me more, tell me more!

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Alright then... Well, I've heard it mentioned that the Jademouth was left behind by Rex Lapis when he marched through here to save the people of Chenyu Vale. Legend has it that to prevent a naval advance from downstream, the local adepti...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: You're making it up as you go again, gramps! There's no way that Liyue's navy came up this river! I've heard that the Jademouth was formed by a piece of jade left behind by a giant Carp!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: In those days, a baddie god tried to redirect the river to drown the Millelith stationed on both of the banks in Chenyu Vale, but a giant white snake and a giant Carp who were her subordinates disobeyed her orders. The giant white snake held up the baddie god, while the giant Carp...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: She threw the jades she wore here. The jades pinned the river down, and ever since, we've had no more floods, and everyone can live peaceful lives on both sides of the river.

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Hehe, you might understand a lot kiddo, but you haven't seen much. Take a closer look — there aren't any crops by this river!

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: See, after it was pinned down by the jades, it's true that the river hasn't flooded... But that's also meant it hasn't been able to provide irrigation for crops! So what was once a wide, gently-flowing river is today a narrow, rapid-flowing torrent instead.

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Such a river leaves no sustenance for the earth on its banks. Haha, and of course that also means no people living peaceful lives on both its sides...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets it now... But did you just say that the adepti were resisting the Lord of Geo, Little Mao?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: That's how it was, all that time ago... Some people believe that the first lord of all Liyue was Rex Lapis. But in Chenyu Vale, we believe that before he came, there were other gods and adepti who protected our ancestors.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: I've heard Grandpa Lu say that the tea ceremony is actually for the Carp adeptus who planted our first tea tree!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh... But aren't these adepti meant to be the baddies? They were serving under a baddie god, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: In some stories they're the baddies, while in others they're the goodies. But it was all such a long, long time ago. Even the grown-ups don't remember much, so they always try to bluff me.

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Hehe... Talking about that friend of yours again? *sigh* How can such supernatural beings be held to our simple codes of right and wrong? As far as we're concerned, all the forces that have ever blessed and protected this land deserve our offerings.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Aaaah, there you go again!

dialogues.speaker: Bosu
dialogues.text: Hahahaha! Alright then, time to get off — we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao and Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, gramps!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Eh? We're not boarding? Well, guess we can just follow the riverbank instead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The terrain here is pretty tough! Aren't you scared of danger, Little Mao?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Of course I am! But... I guess it's because you're afraid that you can bravely climb, right? If you weren't scared at all, you wouldn't care about what kind of roads or stones you tread on. Wouldn't that be more dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, Paimon scared of these mountain roads even without worrying about all that...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hahaha, are you afraid you'll fall off?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's... worried about {NICKNAME}! Yeah, that's right!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I've heard that the Jademouth was formed by a piece of jade left behind by an adeptus named Fujin...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: In those days, the local god — a real baddie, of course — tried to redirect the Bishui River to flood both banks in Chenyu Vale, but an adeptus who was her subordinate, Fujin, disobeyed her orders and threw the jades she wore here.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: The jades pinned the river down, and ever since, we've had no more floods, and everyone can live peaceful lives on both sides of the river.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Fujin...? Paimon thinks we've met her...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Oh? So she was the adeptus you met?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. She even asked us to perform a bunch of errands for her. Said she wanted our help solving Qiaoying Village's problems. According to her, things could get ugly if those issues keep piling up!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Huh... I see...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Shall we go?

choices.text: Aye.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Alright then!

choices.text: I want to take another look around.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Sure. Remember to let me know when you're setting off.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: You know, we might be able to call the whirlpool forth if we try using that adeptal energy!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: You're back, shall we go?

choices.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's be off, fellow spelunkers!

choices.text: Give me a moment. Let's see if there are any treasure chests that we haven't found yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously? There's no helping you, huh? Hang on a moment, alright, Little Mao?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Okay! The cavern's pretty dark, so you've gotta be careful!
